title: New canonical module jnwb/artifact_repair.py: cross-channel-synchrony detection + cross-trial-median substitution for raw LFP trial segments, wired into extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py
notes: Overnight autonomous build (Hamm away). Consolidates two prior one-off artifact findings -- lfp-movement-artifact-v198o-v182o-20260806.json (raw-LFP movement artifact, two validated detector families) and tonight's TFR-domain fig_v1_omission_band_dynamics/band_power_dynamics.py::repair_band_artifacts (cross-trial-median substitution pattern) -- into one importable module operating on the (n_trials, n_channels, n_times) contract every extraction script already uses.

METHOD: per trial, per channel, robust z of that channel's own within-trial values; synchrony[trial,time] = median over channels of |z| (cross-channel-synchrony statistic, geometry matches raw-LFP artifacts being synchronous ACROSS CHANNELS WITHIN A TRIAL, per the 2026-08-06 lab record). Flag (trial,time) where synchrony > Z_THRESH=6.0 AND not within REWARD_WINDOW_MS=(4000,4300) of trial onset (reward-locked transient, a documented separate phenomenon, excluded not repaired). Flagged cells substituted with the cross-trial median at that time across ALL channels -- the same 'repair_band_artifacts' substitution pattern, applied to raw amplitude instead of TFR power.

DELIBERATE THRESHOLD CHOICE, STATED: Z_THRESH=6.0 is the CROSS-CHANNEL-SYNCHRONY detector's validated threshold from the 2026-08-06 lab record (repair_lfp_movement_artifacts.py's own Z_THRESH). That record ALSO validates a differently-scaled 'cross-trial-median' detector at z=15 (per-channel-pooled MAD, heavy-tailed statistic) -- NOT the same number, NOT interchangeable; the record explicitly documents that threshold does not transfer between the two differently-constructed z-scores. This module uses the cross-channel-synchrony geometry (z=6) for detection because that is the geometry raw-LFP movement artifacts actually have (synchronous across channels), then substitutes via cross-trial median (not the prior script's linear-interpolation repair) per direct instruction to match band_power_dynamics.py's pattern 'in spirit'. This is therefore a third, new variant -- not a straight reuse of either prior script -- documented as such in the module docstring.

SELF-TEST: synthetic (20 trials, 8 channels, 200 samples) array, one obvious cross-channel-synchronous spike injected at trial 7 (~40x noise SD, all channels) -- detector flagged it (synchrony z_max=27.2), repair substituted only that cell, all other trials byte-identical to input. Second self-test confirmed a spike placed inside a declared reward window is correctly excluded from repair. Both assertions pass (python jnwb/artifact_repair.py, printed PASSED both times).

WIRED IN: scripts/extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py::extract_channel_segments now repairs the local 3-channel window (loaded for Laplacian referencing) BEFORE re-referencing, for every trial, every cell. Stated limitation: synchrony statistic here uses only 3 local channels (the window already loaded for Laplacian re-referencing), not the full probe (~128 channels) -- weaker detector than a full-probe scan, not hidden.

SMOKE TEST: --limit-sessions 1 completed in 54s (vs unrepaired baseline ~9.5s/session per the 2026-07-30 README timing, 142s/15 sessions) -- repair adds real per-cell cost (~5.7x/session). Corpus-wide run (21 readiness-gated sessions) estimated ~19 min, well inside an overnight window; launched in background (see extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py's own run log outputs/lfp_coupling_matrices/run_repaired_20260813.log).
issues: Only probe_0/the loaded 3-channel window is scanned per cell in the extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py integration, not a full-probe synchrony scan -- if a future robustness check wants the strongest available detector, repair_lfp_movement_artifacts.py's session-wide, all-probe, cached synchrony-z arrays remain the more sensitive alternative (different repair style: linear interpolation, not cross-trial median).

Not yet wired into extract_spike_lfp_coupling.py (PPC-based fig07 pipeline is being replaced, not extended, by scripts/extract_within_session_spk_lfp_sliding_corr.py -- that new script uses band_power_dynamics.repair_band_artifacts on the TFR-domain input instead, a documented, separate artifact-repair path for a differently-shaped input).
plan: Once the corpus-wide repaired LFP-LFP rerun finishes, compare against the original 2026-08-05 null (imaginary coherency, 0/240 Holm/BH) via scripts/aggregate_lfp_lfp_coupling_corrected.py and record the comparison as its own node.

verification.receipt: jnwb/artifact_repair.py (self-test in __main__ block, run via `python jnwb/artifact_repair.py`); scripts/extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py --limit-sessions 1 (54s, 300 results written to outputs/lfp_coupling_matrices/coupling.npz)
